_comment: Manifest for radio/tools/make_sounds.py. Every file lands in
sdcard/SOUNDS/en/WLR/ as 32 kHz 16-bit mono PCM, which is what EdgeTX
wants. Basenames are 8 characters or fewer so the Special Function
'Play Track' picker can browse them too, not just Lua playFile().
The state and fault basenames are NOT free-form: they must match the
wav fields in WIDGETS/WLRHUD/robotdef.lua, which is generated from
firmware/robot_teensy/protocol/schema.json. make_sounds.py cross-checks
them and fails if they drift.
Edit the 'say' strings freely -- they are only the words. Re-run
make_sounds.py after any change.
Copies of a few sounds into /SOUNDS/en/ itself, named 6 characters or
fewer. EdgeTX Special Functions pick a track from the top of the
language folder, and cannot reliably reach into the WLR/ subfolder --
so the handful of sounds driven by Special Functions rather than by Lua
get a flat copy here. dest -> source basename.
Every name is wlr-prefixed on purpose. The stock EdgeTX sound pack
already ships armed.wav and disarm.wav in this folder, and other models
on the radio use them. Copying over those would silently change what
an unrelated model says.
Lua uses the WLR/ folder with full paths and is unaffected.
Alert tones, synthesised. 'segs' is a list of segments:
[freq_hz, ms]                     -- steady tone
[freq_hz, ms, end_freq_hz]        -- linear sweep
[0, ms]                           -- silence
'gain' scales the final peak (1.0 = -3 dBFS).
